FICTIONAL TEST REPORT
CLINIC LETTER
Date of clinic: 29/08/2025
Clinic: Cardiology outpatients (fictional)
Diagnosis: Mitral valve prolapse with moderate mitral regurgitation.
Dear Doctor,
Thank you for asking me to review this patient, aged 54, who attends with palpitations occurring about twice a week, each lasting 2 to 3 minutes, with no syncope or chest pain. Her exercise tolerance is unchanged at roughly 400 metres on the flat.
On examination the pulse was 72 beats per minute and regular, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg. There was a mid-systolic click followed by a grade 2/6 apical pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla. The chest was clear and there was no peripheral oedema.
Echocardiography today showed prolapse of the posterior mitral leaflet with moderate eccentric regurgitation, progressed from mild on the study of 14/02/2023. The left atrium measures 46 mm and the ejection fraction is 62 percent.
PLAN:
1. Continue bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
2. 24 hour ambulatory ECG monitor to be arranged.
3. Repeat echocardiogram in 12 months, sooner if symptoms worsen.
4. Review in clinic after the monitor results.
Yours sincerely,
[fictional clinician], Consultant Cardiologist
